_comment: Project-level converter configuration. Committed with the defaults of the suite this converter was first built on; override per machine with a sibling converter.config.local.json (gitignored) or --config <path>. Every key is optional and deep-merges over these values. Keys starting with _ are documentation.

placeholder_aliases._comment: Placeholder spellings Config.LEGACY_ALIASES resolves to the same key. Folded to the canonical form before a template body is hashed so two bodies that make an identical request are one file. Only pairs Java already treats as equal.

diagrams._comment: Per-test-case Mermaid flowcharts under _flows/<suite>/cases/*.md are always written. The png block renders each of them to an image as well.

_keys.enabled: true to render images on every convert (or pass --diagram-png for one run)
_keys.scale: device scale factor for png; 2 is crisp on high-DPI screens
_keys.cases: '*' for every case, a glob like 'B2B-5264*', a regex prefixed with 're:', or a JSON list of names/globs
_keys.renderer: auto (mmdc if on PATH, else Python Playwright + Chromium), mmdc, or playwright
_keys.output_dir: where the images go; {suite} is replaced with the suite name

project._comment: How ReadyAPI case names are read. The ticket regex must capture (ticket)(remainder); the ticket is dropped from generated test names and kept in the audit. Product-line tokens are stripped from names so siblings share a class; partners map a token in the case name to the CSV partner column.

assertions._comment: What happens to a ReadyAPI assertion the converter cannot translate. It is always reported -- audit row, LOG.warn, and the original script as an Allure attachment -- but by default the test still PASSES, which means it validates less than the ReadyAPI case did and nothing in a green run says so.

_keys.fail_on_unconverted: true records a soft-assert failure where an assertion could not be translated, so a test cannot report green on coverage it does not have. Off by default: turning it on fails every case carrying one, which is the honest state but not a change to make silently on an existing suite.

identity._comment: The Properties vocabulary the identity regeneration owns: what ReadyAPI's DataGen script writes per run and what the framework therefore regenerates. Names are matched case-insensitively where the code says so. The Java runtime reads these through the emitted src/main/resources/converter_identity.json.

_keys.standard_fields: fields every DataGen pack writes; generated in this order
_keys.regen_trigger_keys: a request referencing one of these (lower-cased) Properties fields gets a fresh identity pack first
_keys.identity_hints: a Groovy setPropertyValue target containing one of these is identity data, not a literal
_keys.id_hint_fields: a CSV column whose field tail contains one of these is a live id and is rewritten to a placeholder
_keys.id_param_names: exact path-parameter / body field names that carry a resource id: a baked-in 6+ digit value there is a stale fixture and becomes a live placeholder
_keys.frozen_domain_key: the Properties key ReadyAPI keeps fixed across runs
_keys.allowed_domains_config_key: program_configuration / -D key holding the comma-separated allowed identity domains
_keys.member_enroll_step_patterns: matched on the step name lower-cased without punctuation; 'a+b' means contains both
_keys.fixture_literal_fields: field -> regex: a saved value matching it is a pre-existing fixture and is never generated or rewritten

heuristics._comment: Project-specific validation rules the emitter and runtime honour.

_keys.pad_width: a JDBC code column shorter than this is left-padded with zeros
_keys.code_like: column / variable name fragments that identify a one-time code
_keys.code_exclusions: a name containing 'code' but also one of these is a property/brand/rate code, not padded
